decisions.reason: As a clearly presented product line that builds directly on the firm’s core geospatial integration capabilities, it is likely meeting at least provisional aspirations and is worth retaining given the firm’s R&D orientation and available slack.

The digital twin service fits the firm’s strategic direction but, with only limited early market visibility and a more uncertain demand profile, management would keep it for now while monitoring whether results rise to aspiration levels.

Authentication and identity delegation are close complements to the firm’s enterprise GeoIT offer, so despite some uncertainty and possible overlap with other identity products, the product is likely to be retained while its performance becomes clearer.

An open GIS application development framework is highly consistent with the firm’s long-term platform strategy and customer-specific solution business, making early withdrawal unlikely even if short-term results are still forming.

Because the GIS-specific identity and access service directly supports integration of GeoIT applications and was explicitly introduced as a new service, management would likely keep it unless subsequent results fall clearly below aspirations.
